title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is grappling with a mix of funding boosts and operational challenges, while the military continues to expand its partnerships with private firms. As the satellite sector faces its most costly issues on the ground, new technologies and collaborations are emerging to address the evolving landscape.

themes.title: Funding for Future Tech
themes.body: Venus Aerospace's recent $91 million raise underscores the ongoing interest in advanced propulsion technologies. Meanwhile, the Space Force's budget markup hints at a strategic pivot toward enhancing space resilience.

themes.title: Tactical Collaborations Grow
themes.body: The partnership between Anduril and L3Harris on a tactical SDA constellation bid illustrates the increasing convergence of defense and commercial space capabilities. Such collaborations are likely to shape future military operations in orbit.

themes.title: Strained Spaceports in Focus
themes.body: The government is exploring options to alleviate pressure on spaceports, which have become critical yet strained infrastructure. This could signal a shift in how launch operations are managed as demand continues to rise.

themes.title: Satellite Industry's Ground Woes
themes.body: Despite advancements in satellite technology, the industry faces significant challenges on the ground, particularly related to costs and logistics. Addressing these issues may prove more complex than the launches themselves.
